issues: No sign of gaming the measurement. Scaffold counts and sample weights use train_smiles only. Nothing reads files, pastes answers or uses test labels.

No bug that would make the result meaningless. The weights are 1/count of each Murcko scaffold, normalised to mean 1, and are passed correctly to XGBRegressor.fit. The scaffold SMILES are only used as dictionary keys, so the kekulisation and canonicalisation details don't matter.
Small robustness risk: if Chem.MolFromSmiles returns None, MurckoScaffoldSmiles fails. The job ran without crashing, so this is not a problem on this data.

Recomputed z: the candidate (0.4784) is 0.0066 worse than the incumbent (0.4718). With one run each and a noise sd of 0.0070, the sd of the difference is 0.0070*sqrt(2) ≈ 0.0099, so z ≈ -0.667. This matches the harness value of -0.661 within rounding. It is not significant and points in the wrong direction, so rejecting is correct.
